items.title: An old laptop from my drawer became my first home server, running Docker, Jellyfin, and Immich without buying anything
items.summary: When I built my DDR5 PC with a Ryzen 5 7600X and an RTX 4070 Ti Super, I saw less and less of my Lenovo Legion 5 Pro laptop that carried me through university. For the first month, I'd use it every once in a while to look up and migrate files that I needed, but over the next few years, it became something I'd only open to look back on my work or share photos with friends and family.

items.title: I use ZFS in my homelab, and I wish these 5 myths would go away
items.summary: If you have ever considered using ZFS for your home server, you have probably encountered some rather intimidating advice. Apparently, you need enterprise grade hardware, enormous amounts of RAM, and a server motherboard before you should even think about creating your first pool. Reading some discussions, you would think ZFS was designed exclusively for people who have a server rack in their basement.

items.title: Pulse Monitors Your Proxmox and Docker Servers From One Dashboard
items.summary: Keeping an eye on a homelab gets more complicated once you have several machines running different services. Your Proxmox dashboard might show that everything is online, while a Docker container on another server has stopped responding. You could also have a backup that's been failing for days without realizing it. Pulse is a self-hosted monitoring application that collects information from your servers and displays it through a central dashboard. It supports Proxmox, Docker, TrueNAS, and several other platforms, with notifications for problems that might otherwise go unnoticed.

items.title: FreeHire Is an Open-Source Job Search Engine You Can Self-Host
items.summary: Job hunting can get messy pretty quickly. Between searching multiple job boards, checking company career pages, tailoring resumes, and keeping track of applications, there's a lot to manage. FreeHire is an open-source job search platform that brings these activities together, with a searchable job database and tools for managing the application process. Finding Jobs Directly From the Source FreeHire collects job listings from company career pages and applicant tracking systems (ATS) such as Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, and Ashby.

items.title: DroppedNeedle Is a Self-Hosted Music Request and Discovery App
items.summary: Running your own music server is great, but finding new albums, downloading them, and getting everything properly organized can still involve quite a bit of manual work. Even with something like Jellyfin or Navidrome handling playback, managing the music that actually ends up in your library is another story. DroppedNeedle aims to simplify that process by bringing music requests, downloads, discovery, and library management into one self-hosted interface. Music Requests and Library Management DroppedNeedle is an open-source music management application that uses MusicBrainz to search for artists, albums, and individual tracks.

items.title: New elementary school planned for northwest Surprise after voters approve $71 million Dysart bond
items.summary: A new elementary school is coming to northwest Surprise after voters approved a $71 million bond for Dysart Unified School District, providing funding to address overcrowding as thousands of new homes continue to reshape the area. The passage of Proposition 421 will help fund construction of a new elementary school in the Asante area, where families say rapid population growth has already forced students to travel farther from home to attend school. For parents like Cameryn Smith, the daily commute has become a major challenge.

items.title: Shelly 3.3.1 Arch Linux Package Manager Improves AppImage Updates
items.summary: Shelly 3.3.1 has been released as the latest maintenance update to the graphical package manager for Arch Linux and Arch-based distributions. The most significant change concerns AppImage management. The Upgrade All button on the AppImage page now performs a fresh update check through Shelly’s command-line interface whenever clicked, rather than relying on results from an earlier scan. Additionally, a new setting, “Always Recheck AppImage Updates on Upgrade All,” lets users control this behavior.

items.title: Empty ATC Tower At Hollywood Burbank Airport Leaves Pilots To Clear Own Takeoffs & Landings
items.summary: Pilots flying into and out of Hollywood Burbank Airport (BUR) had to coordinate their own takeoffs and landings on Wednesday evening after the airport's control tower went 'ATC Zero,' meaning no controllers were on duty. ATC recordings captured pilots from Southwest Airlines and Alaska Airlines announcing their positions to each other over a shared radio frequency, a procedure normally reserved for airports without a control tower.

items.title: AMD AI Engine "AIE" Driver Posted For Mainline Linux Kernel Review
items.summary: Separate from the existing AMDXDNA accelerator driver in the Linux kernel for Ryzen AI NPUs, on Wednesday AMD posted patches for the new AMD AI Engine "AIE" accelerator driver. The AMD AI Engine driver is for enabling the AIE found within Versal adaptive SoCs. The AMD AI Engine on Versal SoCs is a 2D array of VLIW SIMD vector processors for DSP, machine learning, and other use cases. Until now there hasn't been a driver in the mainline Linux kernel for supporting the Versal AI Engine. With Versal SoCs there can be "10s to 100s" of the AI Engines per system/device.

The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

But as he tears through street gangs, the elite, and New York City’s supernatural underworld in pursuit of her killer, a chance at a real life forces him to choose: walk away from ultimate power, or become the very monster he hunts.”

items.title: Raspberry Pi SBCs get an open-source hardware I2C TPM 2.0 security module (Crowdfunding)
items.summary: ANAVI I2C TPM 2.0 is an open-source hardware I2C TPM 2.0 security module for Raspberry Pi single board computers based on the Infineon Optiga SLB 9673 TPM 2.0 chip. It’s an alternative to the earlier ANAVI TPM 2.0 module using an Optiga SLB 9672 SPI chip. The add-on board is designed for developers, hobbyists, and professionals who require enhanced security for Raspberry Pi-based projects. It’s especially useful for disk encryption, secure key storage, and cryptographic operations, but can also work as a True Hardware Random Number Generator (TRNG) for security-critical applications.

items.title: Recall petition filed against El Mirage vice mayor as residents clash over her leadership
items.summary: A group of El Mirage residents is moving forward with an effort to recall Vice Mayor Jacquelyn Parsons, accusing her of failing to deliver on campaign promises. But supporters of Parsons are pushing back, calling the effort a political power play. Recall organizers submitted their petition Tuesday after collecting more than 720 signatures, exceeding the 647 required to potentially trigger a recall election. For residents leading the effort, the petition is about holding elected officials accountable.

items.title: External sandboxes for coding agents
items.summary: External sandboxes for coding agents I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a machine. I worked on this project with Prime Radiant, the AI research lab behind Superpowers and other projects. My post on the Prime Radiant blog introduces the external sandbox pattern, where code executed by the agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox while the agent itself lives outside of that sandbox.

items.title: More ASUS & ASRock Motherboards Seeing Sensor Monitoring Support With Linux 7.5
items.summary: A number of patches were recently queued into the Linux hardware monitoring subsystem's "hwmon-next" Git branch of expanded ASUS and ASRock motherboard support for the upcoming Linux 7.5 kernel. With most of the desktop motherboard vendors not contributing directly to the Linux kernel, in 2026 it's still sadly a matter of independent users working on the sensor monitoring support for their motherboards -- typically just confirming the sensors work and basic patches adding new device/model IDs and at times other basic changes for acknowledging the board has specific sensors.

items.title: Flipper One – A Rockchip RK3576-powered portable Arm Linux computer and networking multi-tool (Crowdfunding)
items.summary: Flipper Devices has launched the Flipper One open-source hardware portable Arm Linux platform and networking/Edge AI multi-tool powered by a Rockchip RK3576 octa-core Arm Cortex-A72/A53 SoC. It also features a Raspberry Pi RP2350 microcontroller for low-level control. You may think of it as a successor to the popular STM32-based Flipper Zero hardware and wireless hacking tool, but the company stresses that the Flipper One is NOT a replacement for the Flipper Zero.

items.title: 7 Open Source Speech to Text Tools for Linux (Local AI Dictation)
items.summary: Typing is a fine way to write and a slow way to catch a thought. The most ground-breaking ideas show up while your hands are busy with a soldering iron, a sleeping cat, or a half-eaten taco. Voice input apps overcome that problem because you talk, and it turns your speech into text. Most of the apps in this list are open source, run on Linux, and drop the text into whichever window has focus. That could be a browser tab, a terminal window, or a notes app. Because most of them can run the speech recognition locally on the machine, nothing you say gets sent anywhere.

items.title: AOPA Calls for Clearer Ground Stop Guidance for GA Pilots
items.summary: The FAA’s nationwide ground stop on Nov. 13 exposed a communication gap for general aviation pilots, many of whom were left unsure whether they could continue flying or needed to land, according to the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association (AOPA). The ground stop, issued shortly before 4 p.m. EST, followed a telecommunications failure that affected air traffic control facilities across the country. The disruption halted departures for more than four hours and raised questions about how the FAA communicates systemwide restrictions to pilots outside the airline environment.

items.title: Microsoft Releases Azure Linux 4 as a Production-Ready Distribution
items.summary: Microsoft has announced the general availability of Azure Linux 4, marking the shift of its Fedora-derived, open-source Linux distribution from public preview to a production-ready operating system for Azure workloads. The release is now officially supported for Azure Virtual Machines and Virtual Machine Scale Sets, with container images also reaching GA. As you may recall, Azure Linux 4 became publicly accessible in June with downloadable ISO images that allowed users to install and test the distribution outside Microsoft’s cloud.

items.title: FAA Proposes Requiring Electronic Payments for Fees and Penalties
items.summary: The FAA is proposing to eliminate paper payment options for a range of aviation-related fees and civil penalties, bringing its regulations in line with the agency’s existing electronic payment practices. The proposed rule, published Nov. 17 in the Federal Register, would require electronic payments for services including aircraft registration, recording aircraft ownership and security documents, replacement airman and medical certificates, and certain civil penalties. The changes would also apply to overflight fees and FAA certification services performed outside the U.S.

items.title: FAA Clears Flight School to Conduct Check Rides for Outside Students
items.summary: Paragon Flight Training has become the first U.S. flight school to receiv e FAA authorization to conduct pilot certification check rides for students outside its own training program. The Fort Myers, Florida-based school received an Airman Certification Organization Designation Authorization (AC ODA) effective Nov. 11, allowing it to administer practical tests for students from flight schools nationwide. The FAA designation was announced Nov. 18 by Paragon President Chris Schoensee. The authorization addresses limited access to Designated Pilot Examiners (DPEs).

items.title: High Sierra Storm — John Muir Trail Day 20
items.summary: The rain fell off-and-on throughout the night. It was a light rain, as I discovered when I left my cabin to pee. It felt like the threat of a serious storm may have been overblown, to coin a pun. Lying warm in my cozy bed in Red’s Meadow, I tried to discern whether I was dreaming (asleep) or daydreaming (awake). I was thinking about the pleasures of life and the inevitability of death. items.title: Why more Maricopa County mail ballots were rejected compared to 2022
items.summary: Maricopa County supervisors are questioning the signature-verification process for mail ballots after this years election had a higher rejection rate than the previous gubernatorial election. The Board of Supervisors voted unanimously Wednesday to certify the election results, sending them on to next weeks statewide canvass. Several supervisors slammed Heap for not attending the county canvass and answering questions like officials from the countys Election Department, a separate office from the Recorders Office.

items.title: NASA Sets Coverage for Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Launch, Prelaunch
items.summary: NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST, Sunday, Nov. 29, for the next launch delivering science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station. The agency also will hold a prelaunch media teleconference on Monday, Nov. 23. Filled with approximately 11,000 pounds of cargo, the Northrop Grumman Cygnus XL spacecraft, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

items.title: Multikernel Linux Comes To ARM64, mklinux 7.0-mk5 Released
items.summary: The out-of-tree Multikernel Linux patches for allowing multiple independent kernel instances to run on the same physical machine is out with a new version. The multi-kernel architecture is interesting for fail-safe kernel purposes, running an RT kernel on certain CPU cores and other non-traditional compute purposes. Multikernel was also demonstrated recently with Kmorph for reboot-less Linux kernel crash recovery. Out now is mklinux 7.0-mk5 as the latest iteration of these Multikernel patches based atop the upstream Linux 7.0 kernel.

items.title: FAA Technician Only Unlocked The Door: Inside The Oversight Gap Behind The Nationwide Ground Stop

We quickly learned that this happened because L3Harris, a government contractor, was doing maintenance to switch telecommunications lines from copper to fiber.

items.title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
items.summary: Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all. The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with.

items.title: White Sands National Park: Things to Do & Where to Camp Nearby
items.summary: Picture this: you wax up a plastic saucer, push off the top of a sugar-white dune, and look up mid-run to see the jagged San Andres Mountains stretched across the horizon. Then you hike back up and do it again. And again, until the sun slips behind those peaks and the whole dunefield glows pink and gold. That’s what happens White Sands National Park, which protects much of the world’s largest gypsum dunefield: 275 square miles of glittering sand in southern New Mexico’s Tularosa Basin. The sand stays cool under bare feet even on warm days, the Sacramento Mountains light up at sunset, and once it’s dark, the stars put on a show of their own.

items.title: NASA Announces Mid-Power Electric Rocket Challenge for US Companies
items.summary: 2 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA launched a new competition inviting U.S. companies to produce prototypes of mid-power Hall effect thrusters – a type of electric propulsion system considered crucial for future space operations and exploration. Hall effect thrusters use an electric field to accelerate a propellant gas, producing efficient thrust for long-duration missions. Used for propelling satellites and deep space robotic vehicles, Hall effect thruster systems are critical technology.

items.title: Water security must remain a top priority in Arizona
items.summary: As Arizonans process the results of our recent election, including a new majority at the state legislature, the seriousness of one issue has not changed: water security. Now more than ever, Arizona must show that it is taking action to ensure long-term water security despite major reductions in a key water supply – the Colorado River. To act, we must accept a new reality: the Colorado River is no longer the dependable water source Arizona relied on for decades, that we invested in and built our water management system around.

items.title: Controllers question official explanation for US air traffic control outage
items.summary: Air traffic controllers and a former senior accident investigator are questioning the US government’s explanation for the November 13, 2026, communications failure that halted departures across the country for more than four hours. Four days after the disruption, the controllers’ union says the FAA has yet to brief its workforce on the specific cause of the outage, and controllers say they want answers. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said it has traced the disruption to excessive data flooding its telecommunications network after contractor L3Harris installed a router at a remote radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas.

items.title: Soverin Suite Joins a Growing Wave of European Companies Selling "Sovereignty as a Service"
items.summary: Switching away from Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace is easy to talk about. Actually doing it is a different story altogether. Somebody has to set up the servers, keep them patched, migrate the mails, and then teach people to use the new software and that's probably the hardest part. That is the gap a new breed of European companies is trying to fill. They don't write the software from scratch. They take open source tools like Nextcloud and Euro-Office, run them on European hardware, and sell it as a ready-to-use service with support in their package.

items.title: Now Nginx Has Critical Vulnerabilities
items.summary: nginx is an open source web server and reverse proxy that sits in front of apps and passes traffic to them, and it is one of the most widely used web servers around. That kind of broad implementation is why a set of ten vulnerabilities fixed in nginx 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 are significant; five of them even let attackers run code on a server. The stable branch gets its fix in 1.30.7 and mainline gets it in 1.31.9; both went out yesterday. Plus, most of the five only matter if a specific feature is in use.

items.title: Sun news: When astronauts caught solar wind on the moon
items.summary: Sun news November 19: The day astronauts caught the solar wind on the moon Today’s top story: Fifty-seven years ago today, on November 19, 1969, Apollo 12 astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean landed on the moon’s Ocean of Storms. It was humanity’s second moon landing. Along with rocks and photos, they collected something unusual: a sample of the sun itself! Here’s how. Our sun constantly blows a stream of particles into space, called the solar wind. On Earth, our magnetic field and atmosphere shield us from it.

items.title: Look out our galaxy’s south window into intergalactic space
items.summary: The 2027 lunar calendar from EarthSky is now available! See the moon’s phase for every day of the year. Get yours now! Gazing toward our galaxy’s south window into intergalactic space When you gaze toward the bright star Fomalhaut, in the constellation Piscis Austrinus the Southern Fish, you’re looking toward what you might call our galaxy’s south window. That is, you’re looking away from the flat plane of our Milky Way, where most of our galaxy’s stars reside. But you’re not looking in complete opposite direction of our galaxy’s core.

items.title: Flexell Space and ALATYR Sign MoU to Explore Solar Power Solutions for Orbital Data Centers
items.summary: Bremen, Germany – Flexell Space, a space energy company, announced that it has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with ALATYR, a French company developing orbital data centers, to explore solar power solutions for space-based computing infrastructure. The collaboration will assess the potential application of Flexell Space’s next-generation solar cell technology to orbital infrastructure designed for large-scale computing and data storage. The companies intend to exchange technical requirements relating to power demand and operating conditions and explore opportunities for future joint development and validation.

items.title: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day nearly 50 years after launch
items.summary: At 5:16:07 AM EST (10:16 UTC) on Nov. 18, and at a distance of 26 billion km from Earth, humanity’s furthest probe, Voyager 1, reached its most notable milestone yet. Nearly 50 years after its launch in September 1977, Voyager 1 reached a distance of one light-day from Earth, the distance light can travel in 24 hours. However, the concept of sending a probe on a “Grand Tour” of the outer planets and eventually into interstellar space dates back to the 1960s. After a storied career exploring space, Voyager 1 deserves a look back at how it got to where it is today, and where it is going.

items.title: Arizona MMR vaccination rates among lowest in the nation and still falling
items.summary: PHOENIX Arizona's measles vaccination rates are declining and rank among the lowest in the country, according to an ABC15 data analysis. Arizona's MMR vaccination rate for kindergartners last school year was 87.4%. The herd immunity threshold for measles is 95%, putting Arizona 7 percentage points below that benchmark and the gap is growing. Fifteen years ago, vaccination rates in Arizona were just above 95%. They have fallen nearly every year since, with the exception of 2020 and 2025. During that same period, the personal and medical exemption rate for kindergartners grew from 5% to over 10%.

items.title: How solar and storage are powering a new era of American manufacturing
items.summary: In the early 2020 s, U. S. Steel launched a nationwide search to find the best location for a new factory. The company had recently completed its acquisition of the Big River Steel mill in Osceola, Arkansas. The goal of the expansion: Replicate the success of Big River Steel, which supplies the automotive, construction, and renewable-energy industries and can produce over 3 million tons of steel annually. After an exhaustive search, the company realized there was no reason to look beyond Northeast Arkansas. ​ “ We went to 48 states and narrowed the site selection down to 20, 10, five, and then three,” said Dan Brown, U.

items.title: Debian Forms New Team to Improve Gaming Hardware Support
items.summary: Debian has announced the creation of a new Gaming Hardware Team whose remit will be to improve Debian’s compatibility with handheld gaming PCs, emulation devices and home consoles. The aim is to make Debian a more viable option for gaming hardware, an area currently dominated by a number of specialist Linux distros. The announcement came from Debian maintainer Aryan Karamtoth, who pointed to the massive strides that Linux gaming has made over the last few years, particularly since the launch of Valve’s Steam Deck.

items.title: Three 'e-waste' Nvidia V100s hit 100 tokens per second on Qwen 3.6 35B in a $1,042 homelab rig
items.summary: A homelab builder benchmarked three used Nvidia V100s on Qwen 3.6 35B, achieving about 100 tokens per second in a custom setup costing $1,042 with just “e-waste” GPUs. The smaller, dense Qwen 3.6 27B manages about 24 tokens per second on the same platform, and the V100s use about half the energy of the same number of P100s for a given job. The blog post, “Scaling ‘E-Waste’: LLMs on Multiple Decommissioned GPUs,” compares nine different builds — one to three K80s, P100s, or V100-16GB cards — on a single Supermicro dual-Xeon board.

items.title: Maricopa County posts fastest election results in 20 years as Recorder Justin Heap skips canvass
items.summary: Maricopa County rejected more than three times as many mail ballots over signature problems this year as in the last midterm, a county supervisor said Wednesday as the Board of Supervisors met to certify the Nov. 3 election results. Supervisor Thomas Galvin, a Republican, said 6,089 ballots were rejected for signatures this year, compared to about 1,800 in 2022. Around the same number of people voted in both elections. “That’s like a tripling number,” Galvin said. “I think we dodged a bullet here because the elections were not close this year.”

items.title: Proton’s Lumo AI chatbot is now available on Linux desktops
items.summary: Proton has released desktop apps for its Lumo AI chatbot on all major desktop OSes, including Linux. Lumo is the Swiss privacy company’s own AI assistant, introduced last year and available to use on line. It offers the same sort of features as other generative AI chatbots, including text and image generation, memory, web searching and editable canvases. It runs on ‘open models’, touts better privacy safeguards and encrypts users’ chat history. It’s free to use (with limits) on a free Proton account.

items.title: ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Lands in Netflix Minigolf With HUNTR/X Courses and New Avatars
items.summary: Netflix Minigolf has just been updated with its first major content drop since launch, adding KPop Demon Hunters courses and avatars to the TV party game. If you've been keeping up with our coverage of Netflix Minigolf, this one won't come as a complete surprise. When the game launched on July 28th with over 60 levels across Stranger Things, Squid Game and Bridgerton, Netflix teased that a KPop Demon Hunters update would follow "later this year." With six weeks of 2026 to spare, it's here. It al…

items.title: Fermi’s 14-Year All-Sky Map Bridges Astronomy’s Elusive "MeV Gap"
items.summary: Gamma rays, the most high-energy type of electromagnetic radiation in the universe, have always had a blind spot. We’ve always had trouble measuring them in the “mega-electron volt” (MeV) energy range, which astronomers have taken to calling the “MeV gap”. But a new paper from an international group of scientists working with the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) Collaboration recently published a paper in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series that takes a stab at closing that gap by identifying 450 cosmic sources in the 20-200 MeV range, providing the clearest view of low-energy gamma rays ever.

items.title: Mysterium VPN on Linux is Strictly for Terminal Junkies
items.summary: Using a VPN, or Virtual Private Network, on your computer hides your real IP address from websites and encrypts your traffic before it leaves your device, while your ISP remains clueless about your online activities. It helps the most on networks you don't control, like public Wi-Fi at a cafe or an airport. There are several VPN services that provide Linux clients. Mysterium VPN is one more name to consider, but its Linux client is a command-line tool, and there's no graphical app. But that's still fine for a seasoned Linux user, I guess.

items.title: Water main leak shuts down stretch of Phoenix roads
items.summary: Traffic restrictions are expected as crews investigate a leak that may involve a 20-inch water main near 7th Avenue and Dobbins Road.

items.title: Safety dispute keeps Buckeye storage units empty
items.summary: A new storage facility in south Buckeye sits unused as the owner and a civil engineer warn of failing second-floor stabilization and water leaks. FOX 10's Nicole Krasean reports.

items.title: How M.C. Escher’s Art Creates Bizarre Mathematical Worlds
items.summary: Maurits Cornelis Escher didn’t plan on becoming the darling of mathematicians. Born in 1898 in the canal-lined city of Leeuwarden in the Netherlands, Escher struggled with mathematics as a student, once remarking that he “never got a pass mark.” He ended up studying decorative arts and printmaking, and he used his artwork to explore the strange rules of nature that he found operating around him. Source…

items.title: This featherweight, flying robot carries its own sensors and computers
items.summary: Over the past decade, MIT researchers have developed aerial microrobots with bumblebee-like speed, agility, and durability, for tasks like precision agriculture or search-and-rescue. But these featherweight microrobots couldn’t carry the electronics needed for navigation, forcing them to remain connected to a motion-capture system in the lab. Now, the researchers have designed a flapping-wing microrobot with onboard sensors and computation, which can follow a complex trajectory and land precisely on a sunflower outside the lab’s motion capture environment.

items.title: SDL Ready For Linux's New Nintendo Switch 2 Controller Driver
items.summary: Introduced in Linux 7.4 is a new driver for the Nintendo Switch 2 controllers that was developed by Valve. The widely-used SDL library used by games for software/hardware abstractions now has added mappings for this driver to ensure the Switch 2 controllers will jive nicely for Linux gaming…

items.title: Google DeepMind Releases Gemini 4 Neon: 1M Context, #1 on AA Coding Agent Index
items.summary: Google DeepMind just released Gemini 4 Neon. Gemini 4 Neon is a reasoning model that sits between Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen. It targets coding agents, knowledge work and science workflows. The developer pitch is near-frontier scores at a lower cost per task. Pricing is $3 per 1M input tokens and $15 per 1M output tokens. TL;DR Size: 1M-token unified context, 64K default output, up to 1M via background long decode. Runs on: Google-hosted only. Closed weights, so no local GPU, quantized or edge builds.

items.title: Three studies examine how autonomous AI reshapes responsibility, expertise and real-world decisions
items.summary: Who is responsible for the actions of an autonomous artificial system, how much authority should be attributed to its judgments, and what changes when it acts in the physical world? The public and scientific debate on artificial intelligence is increasingly focusing on agentic AI (or Agentic AI), namely systems capable of pursuing goals and autonomously deciding which actions to take to achieve them, without requiring human intervention at every step.

items.title: Canonical Academy’s Full SysAdmin Certification Track Is Now Available
items.summary: Canonical Academy (Ubuntu’s certification platform, launched in Oct 2025) now offers all four of its System Administrator exams. As we reported at launch, only the Using Linux Terminal exam was available at that stage. The other two (Using Ubuntu Desktop and Using Ubuntu Server) were in beta, and the fourth was still in development. Now Canonical has confirmed the full line is available: Using Linux Terminal, Using Ubuntu Desktop, Using Ubuntu Server, and Using DevOps Principles. The first exam is all about the basics of the Linux command line, basic system administration, security, and resource management.

items.title: Old infrastructure, AI-driven fixes behind wave of US outages
items.summary: A sudden spate of disruptive tech breakdowns in the United States has triggered widespread public unease and compelled top officials to counter rampant speculation about everything from malicious actors to unchecked AI.

items.title: Porsche’s newest electric car is a tiny 50 mph replica of a legendary racer
items.summary: Porsche’s latest electric vehicle isn’t a new Taycan or Macan EV. In fact, it’s not even a full-sized car. Instead, the German automaker has teamed up with British luxury miniature car builder Hedley Studios to create an 80%-scale electric replica of one of Porsche’s most iconic racing cars, the legendary 550 Spyder. more…

items.title: Gilbert launches water audits at town facilities amid Colorado River concerns
items.summary: GILBERT, AZ Gilbert is beginning water efficiency audits at more than 30 municipal facilities as the town prepares for potential cuts to its Colorado River water supply. The effort comes as town officials consider entering Stage 2 of Gilberts water supply reduction management plan as early as Jan. 1, 2027. Town staff plans to bring the proposal to the Town Council in December. If approved, Stage 2 would call for voluntary water reductions from residents. Theres a lot of uncertainty on the Colorado River, and because of that we are going to be seeing reductions in our Colorado River supply, said Jeremiah Churchill, Gilberts water resources and conservation coordinator.

items.title: What's next for NASA interstellar Voyager 1 probe after passing 1 light-day from Earth?
items.summary: Voyager 1 has reached a historic milestone in space — it now takes a light-day to send a command to the spacecraft, meaning a full 24 hours for Earth to hail the distant spacecraft. Since Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, launched on an initial tour through the outer solar system in 1977, their missions have been packed with science. Voyager 1 looked at Jupiter and Saturn from up close before veering for a flyby of Saturn's moon Titan and Saturn's rings, a pathway that brought it above the plane of the solar system in the early 1980s.

items.title: SwitchBot Hub 4 Smart Home controller supports Matter 1.3, Hello Kata voice control, over 101,000 infrared devices
items.summary: SwitchBot Hub 4 is a Smart Home control hub with a color display, physical controls (buttons and knob), Hello Kata voice control, WiFi and Bluetooth connectivity, and Matter Bridge 1.3 support. It supports over 101,000 infrared appliances, including air conditioners, televisions, projectors, fans, streaming devices (Fire TV, Apple TV, and Android TV), and more. For devices that are not part of the list, you can also use the IR learning function. The hub can also control Bluetooth HID devices, SwitchBot devices, and Matter devices via on-screen touch shortcuts and the rotary knob.

items.title: Astronomers witness a star eating its companion in 1st-of-its-kind observation
items.summary: Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com.

items.title: Fire retardant caused corrosion in firefighting aircraft, NTSB finds
items.summary: A fire retardant approved for use in US firefighting aircraft caused extensive corrosion during a single fire season, damaging wing structures, control cables, electrical connectors and engines, according to a National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) investigation. The findings prompted the NTSB on November 17, 2026, to call for stronger US Forest Service testing requirements. Investigators found that the agency’s approval process had failed to adequately assess how the chemical would affect aircraft under actual operating conditions.

items.title: On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water
items.summary: On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars. The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago. MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars. The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years.

items.title: Yet another satellite company is jockeying for a rocket—but this one makes sense
items.summary: Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe's first true vertically integrated end-to-end space company. The announcement came as an all-cash voluntary tender offer from an Italian subsidiary of ICEYE to Avio's shareholders, led by the Italian defense conglomerate Leonardo. Avio said its board of directors "has taken note of the notice" from ICEYE and is considering the purchase offer.

items.title: Incoming Democratic leader promises a more respectful Arizona Legislature
items.summary: It will be a whole new world in the coming year with Democrats at the helm of the Arizona Legislature, and one of the favorite punching bags for Republicans at Capitol is hopeful that will mean a shift toward collegiality. “By God, I hope it changes the tone,” Jen Marson, executive director of the Arizona Association of Counties, said during a Wednesday Zoom discussion hosted by Arizona State University’s Mechanics of Democracy Lab. Marson has spent the last 20 years advocating for Arizona’s 15 counties at the state legislature.

items.title: Ai2 and Taylor Geospatial partner to make geospatial AI easier to compare, run, and build on
items.summary: Ai2 and Taylor Geospatial are partnering to make geospatial AI more accessible and useful for the public good through open models, shared benchmarks, and improved satellite imagery datasets for applications in conservation, agriculture, and humanitarian work.

items.title: System76’s Redesigned Thelio Prime Linux Desktop Is Now Available
items.summary: System76’s redesigned Thelio Prime Linux desktop is now available, featuring a smaller chassis, updated AMD Ryzen processors, and dedicated graphics options from AMD and NVIDIA. The new model is 48.5% smaller than the original, with an internal volume of 9.78 liters, while retaining desktop-class hardware for productivity and gaming. The most noticeable change is the redesigned enclosure. Built from aluminum and stainless steel, the new Thelio Prime features magnetically attached side panels and a smoked tempered-glass front, making internal components easier to access for maintenance and upgrades.

items.title: As Scandinavian Countries Slowly Converted to Christianity, Crusades Often Took on the Form of Viking Raids
items.summary: In 1107, after the First Crusade, Christians held Jerusalem, and Norway’s King Sigurd set sail to defend the city with 60 ships and around 5,000 men. In northern Spain, Sigurd ended up ransacking the fortress at Compostela, one of Western Europe’s holiest sites. He went on to sack Lisbon, storm Ibiza and Minorca, and then team up with King Baldwin of Jerusalem to conquer the port city of Sidon, in modern-day Lebanon. A grateful Baldwin gave Sigurd a fragment of wood from what he said was Jesus’s cross.

items.title: ForeFlight to Add AI-Powered ATC Transcriptions
items.summary: Jeppesen ForeFlight and Archer Aviation announced a partnership Tuesday to develop real-time air traffic control transcription capabilities for ForeFlight Mobile. According to the companies’ announcement, the proposed feature would use Archer’s ZEE artificial intelligence model to display ATC transmissions as text on an iPad. The integration is currently in the initial testing phase. How the System Would Work Archer said its ZEE model was trained using more than 100,000 hours of actual ATC communications.

items.title: Scottsdale approves arts magnet school at shuttered Echo Canyon campus
items.summary: The Scottsdale Unified School District wants to turn a shuttered school into something it has never had before a school dedicated entirely to the arts. The Scottsdale School Board voted 5-0 Tuesday night to open an arts magnet school at the now-shuttered Echo Canyon campus, near 62nd Street and Camelback Road, targeting the 2028-29 school year. "I'm nervous. I'm legitimately nervous, and I feel contradictory to the whole idea of the school closures we just did. But I'm totally excited about this approach," said Donna Lewis, Scottsdale school board president.

items.title: Helping AI text detectors keep up with changing conditions
items.summary: A teacher who believes a student’s term paper may have been written by a large language model (LLM) can use a tool for detecting artificial intelligence-generated text to help confirm their suspicions. But the teacher may want to think twice before putting all their trust in the detector. Researchers from MIT and Cornell University showed that such detection tools, which are AI models themselves, can be fooled by AI-generated text disguised to appear as if it were written by a human. Detectors can also fail to identify AI text due to natural shifts in writing habits over time or the emergence of new LLMs.

items.title: Fictional Project designs home in Kerala to feel "one with the landscape"
items.summary: Curving ceilings sweep down to frame the two small gardens that flank this home in Kerala, India, designed by local architecture studio Fictional Project. Named Interstitial Living, the home in the village of Adoor was designed for a family of four who wanted to feel connected to the outside, in particular the lush greenery surrounding the site. This led Fictional Project to pull the home's built volume back to create space for two planted yards on either side, overlooked by the home's pared-back and open interiors.

items.title: Meet Swedish Girls, Sabine Marcelis’s pick for the most influential designer of the next 20 years
items.summary: Sabine Marcelis has nominated Swedish Girls as a key name to watch over the next two decades for Dezeen's 20×20 project sponsored by Kohler. In this interview, we learn why the design duo deliberately play into stereotypes. The steady emergence of Swedish Girls has not been lost on prolific Dutch designer Marcelis, who nominated the collective as one of 20 names to watch in architecture and design over the next 20 years. "I really like how they work with existing industrial production processes, yet the result very much speaks to the current culture," Marcelis told Dezeen, explaining her selection.

items.title: The world’s biggest oil shock could give EVs and solar a boost
items.summary: The longer the Strait of Hormuz crisis drags on, the more incentive countries have to get cars off oil and generate more power at home. That’s one of the big takeaways from the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) new “ World Energy Outlook 2026,” which examines how the biggest oil supply shock on record could speed up the shift to EVs and solar. more…

items.title: Waugh Thistleton Architects set to transform derelict bathing pavilion into Tracey Emin-backed studios and sauna
items.summary: UK studio Waugh Thistleton Architects is set to transform the Edwardian Westbrook Pavilion in Margate, UK, into an arts centre for British artist Tracey Emin with a cafe, public sauna and changing rooms. "The project will bring a much-loved seafront building back into use, combining its original purpose with new spaces for art, culture and the local community," said Waugh Thistleton Architects. The studio recently won planning permission from the local council to convert the abandoned building, which Emin purchased in 2023, into a facility run by the Tracey Emin Foundation.

items.title: How AI can identify the magnetic structures behind high-frequency energy loss
items.summary: From electric vehicles to renewable energy systems and data centers, modern technologies depend on efficient power conversion. These systems depend on magnetic components such as transformers and inductors. However, magnetic materials lose energy during operation, generating heat and limiting efficiency. As electrical systems operate at increasingly high frequencies, understanding the microscopic origins of these losses is becoming crucial to improving energy efficiency.

items.title: Hadean Tactics devs announce Black Flame Tactics, a co-op autobattler roguelike
items.summary: If you missed the auto-chess craze and miss stuff like Dota Underlords, perhaps Black Flame Tactics might fill a gaming hole for you. In Black Flame Tactics, players build a party of heroes and lead it to the bottom of the world, where the Black Flame burns. No two runs are the same: new heroes, relics, mysterious events, bosses, ancient pacts and more await on every descent, played solo or with a friend in online co-op.

items.title: Lost Ark unlocks the strongest battle possible against Modrum, the Abyssal Punisher in its newest update
items.summary: Thunder rolls across Arkesia once more, apparently, as players in Lost Ark are able to face off against Mordum, the Abyssal Punisher in Kazeros Raid Act 3 Extreme. Not forever, though, just for four weeks. After four weeks, Mordum will officially feel that the abyss is sufficiently punished. Or maybe other things have been punished and…

items.title: Seaweed earplug among grant-winning Design Museum prototypes
items.summary: A single-use earplug crafted from seaweed, two plant-based insulation materials and a homegrown timber kit-of-parts for low-rise buildings are among the projects that have been awarded Design Museum grants. UK-based studios Searo Labs, WeCanMake, Local Works Studio and SY Ecofit have been granted a share of £280,000 from the Design Museum for their "cutting-edge" environmental prototypes. Described as the "world's first seaweed-based single-use earplug", SearoSoft by Cambridge-based Searo Labs is a fully biodegradable and renewable alternative to single-use earplugs.

items.title: SolarEdge debuts Duo power optimizer at RE+
items.summary: SolarEdge unveiled its new U.S.-made Duo power optimizer for commercial and industrial (C&I) solar projects this week at RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas. Power optimizers are DC to DC converters connected to the underside of solar modules that maximize power output. What sets the new Solar Edge optimizers apart is that instead of needing one per module, one Duo connects to two modules with an independent maximum power point tracker (MPPT) for each module. The company says because of its dual operation, fewer optimizers are needed, making for simplified installation.

items.title: Get some co-op games and stealth action in two new Humble Bundles
items.summary: You can grab two more Humble Bundles with a nice mixture of co-op games to play with friends, and some stealth action games too. As usual from GamingOnLinux, we're here to make it easier for you with Steam links and all the ratings you might need. Don't sleep on Deceive Inc, not a lot of players but really good fun.

items.title: Stem sells battery optimization IP to Voltus as it faces financial difficulties
items.summary: tem has sold the intellectual property behind its Athena distributed battery optimization software to virtual power plant operator Voltus for $10 million in cash. The news was announced alongside Stem’s third-quarter financial results this week. The transaction means the ownership of the dispatch and tariff-optimization software, reportedly deployed across more than 800 battery sites across North America, is now with San Francisco-based Voltus. Stem will still retain the right to license Athena to its existing managed-services customers, while Voltus assumes ongoing platform development and commercialization.

items.title: Tesla crashes make headlines, Lidar makes sense, IONNA makes it easy
items.summary: On today’s high-impact episode of Quick Ch a rge, we’ve got a flurry of fatal Tesla crashes allegedly involving Autopilot and FSD making headlines – and they all feel weirdly familiar. Is there any way to keep this from happening again? As Electrek ‘s ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data continues, a number of recently matched fatal crashes involving Autopilot and/or FSD have been making headlines. In addition to being tragedies, they seem all too familiar, drawing comparisons to older incidents that occurred under similar conditions while raising questions about whether possible solutions might already exist.

items.title: Americans Bought More Used EVs In October. Fewer Of Them Were Teslas
items.summary: U.S. used EV sales hit 48,678 in October, up 73% year over year. Tesla still led despite a 5.4% monthly sales drop. The Equinox EV, EV6 and Leaf gained. Used EV asking prices averaged $36,582 last month. September was a good month to be selling a used Tesla Model Y. Sales jumped nearly 14% from August, and the Ford Mustang Mach-E did even better. The Chevrolet Equinox EV beat both, though, with a nearly 42% increase. A month later, only one of those three electric crossovers was still gaining buyers: the Chevy.

items.title: Putin vows 'far more painful' response to Ukraine's strikes on Crimean Bridge
items.summary: Moscow's retaliation for attacks on the Crimean Bridge will be "far more painful" than Kyiv's strikes, Vladimir Putin has vowed. In the early hours of Thursday, the double-arched, 12-mile bridge connecting Russia to Ukraine's occupied peninsula of Crimea was hit for a third time this week. A combined missile-and-drone strike on Tuesday destroyed the central road section of the bridge, collapsing part of it into the water and rendering it unusable for road traffic. But at a press conference after historic talks with his Chinese and US counterparts in Shenzhen, Russian president Putin said Moscow's response would be even more significant.

items.title: Putting a spotlight on AI, society, and humanity
items.summary: MIT students are going to office hours less often. They’re spending less time working through problem sets, and with one another. Those were among the findings of MIT’s recent report on artificial intelligence and education, and they are one reason a growing number of MIT faculty are concerned about how generative AI is both changing how people work and affecting how they think, learn, and relate to one another. For the MIT Human Insight Collaborative (MITHIC), those questions have become a central focus, and MITHIC is working with collaborators across the Institute, including the Social and Ethical Responsibilities of Computing (SERC), to help MIT address them.

items.title: Tesla’s $30,000 Cybercab comes with a $299 monthly catch
items.summary: There is always a catch. Or in the case of Tesla ’s self-driving Cybercab, several. Last Friday night, Tesla said it had invited “select customers” to purchase their very own Cybercabs. The two-seat, gold vehicle is unlike any other on the market: It lacks a steering wheel and brake pedals, and is primarily driven by software. (Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Alphabet's Waymo and Amazon’s Zoox, offer self-driving rides on ride-hail networks, but don’t let people buy their cars.) Tesla’s " limited release ” will supposedly offer some people (unclear how many) the opportunity to pay $29,900 to take delivery in December.

items.title: New AI method reveals which concepts vision models recognize and where they appear
items.summary: Foundation models are AI models trained on enormous amounts of data that can subsequently be adapted to perform a wide range of tasks—much like an operating system that supports a variety of programs. One type is the language-aligned vision foundation model (VLM), which is trained on millions of image-text pairs, enabling it to connect images with language. Today, they are used in a wide range of applications, from image recognition and image search to image generation, and in combination with large language models.

items.title: Nearly 1 In 5 Tesla Model Ys Failed Their First German Inspection
items.summary: The Model Y ranked last among 109 models. At its first inspection, 18.5% had major defects, nearly triple the 6.4% average for cars of its age. Inspectors flagged worn suspension joints on Model Ys 24 times as often as on comparable cars. The Mazda MX-30 ranked third overall with a 3% failure rate, though it averaged less than half the Model Y’s mileage. Ask a used Tesla buyer what they’d like checked first, and I’m pretty sure the battery would come up pretty quickly. After reading what German inspectors found underneath some surprisingly young Model Ys, I’d want to know how the suspension was holding up, too.

items.title: Miss Konosuba? You Need to Watch Crunchyroll’s Funniest Fall Anime

items.title: 19th-Century Philosopher’s Head Examined

items.title: Wealth and Status of Early Herders Evaluated
items.summary: COPENHAGEN, DENMARK—According to a statement released by the University of Copenhagen, Mikkel Nørtoft of the University of Copenhagen has developed a system using multiple sources of information to reconstruct social status from grave goods. To test the method, data from some 300 Corded Ware culture graves in Bohemia dated to between 4,000 and 5,000 years ago was evaluated. The analyses of the graves were then compared with genetic ancestry and Y-chromosome patterns to track paternal lineages. The estimated ages of the individuals in the study, and their sex and known illnesses, were included as well.

The new direction took him somewhat by surprise, as he realized one day he had been focusing much more on fauna than he had in years past. “I think it has a lot to do with a desire to reconnect with everything that exists independently of human beings,” Cian tells Colossal.

items.title: Stonehenge’s six-ton mystery deepens as scientists narrow their search
items.summary: A major new investigation into Stonehenge’s mysterious six-ton Altar Stone has uncovered fresh clues while ruling out several suspected sources. Once thought to have originated in Wales, the massive sandstone slab is now believed to have come from northeastern Scotland, although researchers have yet to find an exact match.

items.title: ‘Widow’s Bay’ Producer to Showrun Netflix’s Adult Animated ‘Grendel’ Series
items.summary: Netflix today announced a new adult animated series, Grendel, based on the long-running Dark Horse comic book series by Matt Wagner that was, in turn, inspired by the monster from Beowulf. The Emmy Award-winning producer of Widow’s Bay, Bobak Esfarjani ( WandaVision, Alien: Earth ), will showrun, write, and executive produce. The logline reads: “ After the woman he loves is shockingly murdered, Hunter Rose devotes himself to one thing: vengeance. But as he tears through street gangs, the elite, and New York City’s supernatural underworld in pursuit of her killer, a chance at a real life forces him to choose: walk away from ultimate power, or become the very monster he hunts.

items.title: Scientists discover a hidden hereditary form of aggressive prostate cancer
items.summary: Scientists have discovered a rare inherited mutation in the CDK12 gene linked to aggressive prostate cancer, with all five identified carriers developing metastatic disease between ages 44 and 62. The finding could lead to expanded genetic testing, helping families uncover hidden cancer risks and potentially detect the disease while it is still treatable.

items.title: Genie 4 is now available
items.summary: Earlier this year we introduced Project Genie, an experimental research prototype that lets you generate and explore interactive worlds. Early testers told us they wanted deeper control over what happens inside those worlds, and easier ways to build and share them. Project Genie brings together our most advanced world models alongside our Gemini models, empowering you to generate, step inside, and shape worlds directly from your browser. With Genie 4, our most realistic and interactive world model yet, you can now prompt mid-session to change the world you created.

items.title: Pakistan minister to visit India, but no breakthrough expected
items.summary: Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik will travel to India from November 20 to 22 to participate in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Civilizational Dialogue in New Delhi. It marks the first India visit by a Pakistani federal minister since the two nuclear-armed archrivals fought a four-day war last year. The fighting erupted after armed gunmen killed over two dozen tourists, mostly Hindus, in India-administered Kashmir in April 2025. New Delhi accused Islamabad of backing the attack, a charge Pakistan denied.

items.title: ‘Groundbreaking’ Trump-Xi-Putin summit: Five key takeaways
items.summary: The presidents of the United States, China and Russia have declared a shared intent to stabilise energy flows, prevent nuclear proliferation and find mechanisms to work more closely together, at an unprecedented summit in Shenzhen, China on Thursday. The meeting, held on the sidelines of the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) conclave, was the highlight of three days of intense diplomacy in the region, where leaders from multiple countries — including US President Donald Trump — had previously gathered in Manila for other summits.

items.title: Build Training-Ready Physical AI Datasets with Two Prompts in NVIDIA Cosmos
items.summary: World model accuracy starts with high-quality, diverse training datasets. Yet capturing rare defects, nighttime incidents, and other challenging scenarios is... World model accuracy starts with high-quality, diverse training datasets. Yet capturing rare defects, nighttime incidents, and other challenging scenarios is costly and time-consuming. Turning raw data into training-ready datasets adds complexity, particularly when using disconnected tools and manual processes for curation, labeling, generation, and evaluation. NVIDIA technology is helping… Source…

items.title: Is free will an illusion? New brain research reveals a surprising twist
items.summary: New research reveals that the brain makes free choices and forced decisions using surprisingly similar neural processes, with activity building toward a decision before we act. The discovery challenges assumptions about free will while suggesting that our personal preferences and experiences still shape what we choose.

items.title: A 115 million‑year‑old 'algae rebellion' in Portugal's sea cliffs pushes back evolutionary timeline
items.summary: Quite a few scientific discoveries are a product of chance. You set out looking for one thing, but often end up finding something totally unexpected. In micropaleontology, the study of microscopic fossils, this is especially common. You never know what you're going to find until you start examining the samples under the microscope.

items.title: Top U.N. court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
items.summary: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya during its 2017 military operations in northern Rakhine State. Delivering the judgment, Judge Yuji Iwasawa said the scale and nature of the military's actions went "well beyond what would be required to punish the population" and were instead "characteristic of an intent to destroy a substantial part of the group." The judges estimated that around 815,000 Rohingya lived in northern Rakhine State before the operations, and concluded that around 10,000 were violently killed during the 2017 clearance campaign.

items.title: Advancing chip design with OpenAI models
items.summary: OpenAI models optimized circuits used in Jalapeño silicon and improved RISC‑V core designs, showing progress in AI-assisted chip design with GPT‑6 Astra.

items.title: The Search for Cleopatra’s Lost Tomb From Alexandria to Taposiris Magna
items.summary: When Cleopatra VII died in 30 BC, Octavian permitted her burial alongside Mark Antony in a grand royal monument. Over two millennia later, their tomb remains undiscovered because ancient Alexandria’s royal quarter sank into the sea. Modern underwater excavations have failed to find the tomb in the heart of the submerged city, which has led modern excavations to shift thirty miles west to Taposiris Magna. Will archaeologists ever piece together Cleopatra’s final resting place?

items.title: A New Breed of Homesteader Is Turning the Abandoned Shacks of a Previous Era Into a Community in the Desolation of California's Wonder Valley
items.summary: If you drive east through the Mojave Desert on California State Route 62, past the towns of Joshua Tree and Twentynine Palms, you reach a place called Wonder Valley. It’s a 150-square-mile expanse of rock, sand, dust and scrub, surrounded by low, jagged mountain ranges and possessing a desolate beauty. A thousand years ago, this stretch of desert was traversed by small groups of hunter-gatherers—Shoshones, Utes, Paiutes. They were supplanted by Serrano people, who were forcibly removed to reservations in the early 20th century.

items.title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
items.summary: The KFF Health News Minute is available every Thursday via direct download or the RSS feed. Nov. 19 Briah [BREE-ah] Lumpkins [LUMP-kinz] reads the week’s news: Signing up for Obamacare can be complicated, but an “independent assister” can help. Plus, how gun owners facing dementia can stay safe as they experience cognitive decline. Your browser does not support the audio element. Can’t see the audio player? Visit kffhealthnews.org to listen. Nov. 12 Sam Whitehead reads the week’s news: Your phone may know when you’re visiting the doctor, and companies are using that information to sell unproven treatments.

items.title: India's religious make-up - what a new Pew study says about Hindus and Muslims
items.summary: India will remain overwhelmingly Hindu for decades to come, but its religious composition is projected to shift gradually. A new study by the Pew Research Center, projecting the world's religious populations to 2070, estimates that Hindus will make up 76% of India's population by then, down from 79% in 2020, while the Muslim share will rise from 15% to 20%. The shift is rooted largely in differences in age and fertility: Indian Muslims are younger than Hindus and, on average, have more children.

items.title: Scalable photonic quantum computer provides new insights into the fundamentals that shape its performance
items.summary: Photonics-based quantum computers open up new possibilities for investigating highly complex problems in mathematics and have the potential to revolutionize fields ranging from energy and chemical research to secure communications. By utilizing the unusual properties of light particles, they can perform calculations that pose enormous challenges even for the most powerful supercomputers—or remain entirely beyond their reach. At Paderborn University, researchers are now investigating a fundamental question using Germany's first scalable photonic quantum computer, a 'Gaussian boson sampler': which quantum resources are most important for the performance of these devices?

items.title: Unquote
items.summary: “A man is wise with the wisdom of his time only, and ignorant with its ignorance.” — Thoreau “Ignorance is a social creation, like knowledge.” — Michael Smithson…

items.title: Everything New On Netflix In December 2026: Full List Of Movies & TV Shows
items.summary: New month, new stuff to stream on Netflix. And the streamer's December 2026 offerings are robust, with the service looking to end the year on a high note thanks to a fresh batch of original programming, as well as some familiar favorites. Movies, TV shows, documentaries, and even live sporting events, the streamer's got it all. To be sure, Netflix has several big original movies coming our way that month, including director Brad Bird's animated sci-fi noir flick "Ray Gunn" (which boasts a star-studded voice cast that's led by Sam Rockwell and Scarlett Johansson).

items.title: How the 3 Wars of German Unification Caused WWI
items.summary: World War I was not simply caused by the assassination of Austrian Archduke Franz Ferdinand. International hostilities had developed in Europe for decades following the German Wars of Unification. In a campaign lasting from 1864 to 1871, the Kingdom of Prussia under Otto von Bismarck embarked on a campaign of military expansion at the expense of three rivals. The result was the creation of the German Empire in 1871. What came afterwards was imperial ambition and rivalry that divided Europe into a web of alliances until war finally erupted in 1914.

items.title: Mesa dog trainer and rescue dog face long road to recovery after car crash
items.summary: MESA – When Keylee Harvey rescued Rogue about two years ago, she met a dog who was shut down, lacked confidence and rarely showed interest in playing with toys. But Harvey helped Rogue come out of her shell through training, patience and a lot of time together. The two became inseparable. “She’s beautiful. She’s like no other. I couldn’t imagine my life without her,” Harvey said. What began as a rescue grew into a partnership built around training, play and shared adventures. Rogue became Harvey’s constant companion, joining her on trips and spending nearly every day by her side.

items.title: Why don't weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy work for everyone?
items.summary: Why do Ozempic and Wegovy produce dramatic weight loss for some people but disappointing results for others? Scientists are investigating whether the body's hidden energy-saving response could help explain the difference and unlock more effective, personalized weight-loss treatments.

items.title: Congress Moves to Close Aviation Safety Gap After 67 Killed in DC Midair Collision
items.summary: WASHINGTON — Congress has agreed on a key aviation safety provision requiring civilian aircraft to carry systems that allow pilots to detect nearby aircraft, following the fatal midair collision involving an American Airlines (AA) passenger jet and a U.S. Army Black Hawk helicopter near Washington, D.C., on January 29, 2025. The agreement marks a significant step toward addressing a long-standing safety gap in the U.S. aviation system. However, lawmakers have yet to settle the provisions governing military aircraft, which remain a major point of disagreement in the broader aviation safety legislation.
