items.title: FIFA confirms Diallo, Tashima as Infantino’s challengers at 2027 election
items.summary: FIFA president Gianni ⁠⁠Infantino’s re-election bid ⁠⁠will be challenged by the French and Japanese federations’ presidents, Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima, football’s global governing body has confirmed. Former Swiss defender Ramon Vega, who announced his intention to run last month, was not among the candidates FIFA mentioned on Thursday. The ⁠⁠election, set to be held in March 2027, will be the first time Infantino faces a challenger after being re-elected without opposition in 2023. French Football Federation (FFF) president Diallo announced his candidacy on Monday, with the support of ‌‌UEFA member associations represented on the executive committee and the FIFA Council.

items.title: 8 Lost Royal Tombs Archaeologists Finally Discovered
items.summary: Ancient royalty often went to elaborate lengths to celebrate their monumental lives and seal their place in the afterlife. But despite the cost and care involved in their burials, many of their tombs were soon lost and forgotten. Modern archaeologists have discovered some of these tombs, revealing the magnificent wealth of many ancient kings and the lengths they would take to secure immortality. From Howard Carter unsealing Tutankhamun’s tomb to identifying Richard III’s desecrated remains beneath a Leicester parking lot, these are eight lost royal tombs that archaeologists have rediscovered.

items.title: Boeing 777X Pilots Have To Manually Extend The Wingtips Before Takeoff But Not Fold Up After Landing
items.summary: One of the Boeing 777X's most famous new features is its folding wingtips. They're roughly 11 feet (3.5 meters) wide each and are designed to be folded up whilst on the ground, allowing the aircraft to use the same airport facilities as older 777 models. They extend before takeoff and remain fully extended until after landing. Interestingly, it's the pilots' responsibility to extend the wingtips before takeoff, but the wingtips retract automatically after landing as the aircraft decelerates on the runway.

items.title: Buckeye officer injured while trying to stop suspected drunk driver, police say
items.summary: A driver allegedly rammed two police cars, injuring an officer, Buckeye police said.

items.title: 31 Cranberry Recipes for Thanksgiving and Beyond
items.summary: Electric-pink pie, cranberry-mustard chicken, a sweet-tart rum punch, and plenty of reasons to keep a bag on hand past the holiday season. Cranberries are doing a lot more than keeping turkey company. Fresh berries bring a sharp, lip-puckering bite to pies, cakes, and relishes. Dried cranberries deliver little bursts of sweetness to rice dishes and cookies. Even the canned stuff has its moments (see: sweet-and-sour chicken). Cranberries are particularly good at turning themselves into sauce, thanks to their generous supply of natural pectin.

items.title: A convincing vegan meat alternative needs both taste and texture – here’s how food scientists manufacture them
items.summary: This Thanksgiving, you may sit down to a table laden with mashed potatoes, cranberry sauce, vegetables and a golden-brown turkey. And, if you have any vegetarians or vegans in your family, you may even see a plant-based meat alternative. But how do food scientists make something taste and look similar to turkey entirely from plants? Plant-based meat alternatives have become an increasingly prominent part of the food industry, driven partly by concerns about the sustainability of conventional meat production and the search for additional protein sources.

items.title: ‘Insectasy’ – The Film Sales Company Acquires Erotic Bug Horror Pic
items.summary: If you ever looked at insects and found them sexy, apparently, you’re not the only one. ScreenDaily reports that The Film Sales Company has acquired worldwide rights to the erotic bug horror pic, Insectasy. Yes, the film is as weird as it sounds. In Insectasy, Sadie ( Tirion Healy ) struggles to find balance in her life between work, dating, and her erotic obsession with insects, experiencing dreamy fantasies along the way. Lyndall Huber and Emmett Roiko also star. Angus Silver wrote and directed the film.

items.title: Mesopotamian Chronology Refined with Tree Rings and Ice Cores
items.summary: TUCSON, ARIZONA— Phys.org reports that a team of researchers led by Charlotte Pearson of the University of Arizona has refined the timeline for historical events in ancient Mesopotamia. First, the team members radiocarbon dated individual tree rings and analyzed tree ring data from timbers unearthed at archaeological sites in Turkey, in order to calculate precise dates for when the trees were felled. These dates helped the researchers to determine when the buildings had been constructed. Then those dates were linked to historical records from the sites that were tied to specific years in the Assyrian calendar.

items.title: North Korea expanding uranium enrichment facility, UN nuclear watchdog says
items.summary: North Korea is expanding a nuclear facility for enriching uranium, according to the head of the United Nations nuclear watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). An existing facility at the Yongbyon nuclear centre has been further expanded in the last couple of months, IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said on Wednesday. This comes as US President Donald Trump expressed his eagerness to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un while he is in Asia for an APEC leaders’ summit in China.

items.title: Too Heavy For Its Own Wings!? Why The Boeing 737-900ER's Takeoff Roll Is So Long
items.summary: The Boeing 737-900ER was designed to solve a specific problem for airlines. Boeing needed a narrowbody aircraft capable of carrying nearly as many passengers as a Boeing 757 while remaining within the operating economics and fleet commonality of the long-running 737 family.The result was the largest and heaviest member of the Next Generation 737 line, an aircraft capable of moving more than 200 passengers while still fitting into the same airport gates, maintenance systems, and pilot type ratings as its smaller siblings. However, stretching an aircraft originally conceived in the 1960s eventually would create compromises that are difficult to hide.

items.title: New Year’s Eve Turns Deadly for Hollywood Friends In Horror Pic ‘Nepo Babies’
items.summary: Privilege is its own horror, and there’s a new film on the way all about why. Deadline reports that key cast members have wrapped on the horror thriller Nepo Babies, currently shooting in Mexico City. The outlet notes that Nepo Babies is described as “ Entourage by way of David Lynch” and “unfolds over a New Year’s Eve pregame in Los Angeles, following a close-knit circle of privileged young Hollywood friends whose glamorous celebration takes a sinister turn when an unwelcome outsider arrives.” Okay, but now I wish Lynch were around to direct an episode of Entourage.

items.title: Trump Administration OKs Native Traditional Healing for Two States’ Medicaid Programs
items.summary: The Trump administration has approved two states’ requests to expand Medicaid to cover Native American traditional healing practices, even as it prepares to enforce rules that are expected to drop millions of people from the government health insurance program. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced in September that the federal agency had approved traditional healing programs for Utah and Maine. The agency did so through waivers, which give a state permission to pay for certain programs that normally fall outside of Medicaid’s rules.

items.title: The First Friend
items.summary: When Wild Dog reached the mouth of the Cave he lifted up the dried horse-skin with his nose and sniffed the beautiful smell of the roast mutton, and the Woman, looking at the blade-bone, heard him, and laughed, and said, ‘Here comes the first. Wild Thing out of the Wild Woods, what do you want?’ Wild Dog said, ‘O my Enemy and Wife of my Enemy, what is this that smells so good in the Wild Woods?’ Then the Woman picked up a roasted mutton-bone and threw it to Wild Dog, and said, ‘Wild Thing out of the Wild Woods, taste and try.’

items.title: Walmart hikes outlook as CEO tells CNBC retailer aims to keep prices low despite soaring fuel costs
items.summary: Walmart on Thursday reported earnings and revenue that narrowly topped estimates and raised its full-year outlook as it saw strong e-commerce growth ahead of the busy holiday season. Walmart said global e-commerce sales grew 17%, driven by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery, with Walmart U.S. up 23% and Sam's Club U.S. rising 30%. Its Walmart U.S. advertising business saw a 37% sales increase for the quarter. Walmart said it rolled back prices on nearly 8,000 products across its stores, a focus as U.S. consumers worry about the cost of living in the face of elevated food and gas prices.

items.title: Academy Museum Unveils Winter Program, Including Tribute to Hammer Horror Films!
items.summary: The Academy is about to become the Hammer House of Horror. Variety reports that the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures, located here in Los Angeles, has announced their winter programming…and it features a few horror entries of note. On December 5th, audiences can attend “Inside Horror: Frightening Sounds With Karen Baker Landers”, followed by “Dark Entries: The Birth of Horror Cinema”, running from December 7th to February 26th. January sees the genre selections pick up, with Jan.

items.title: Yahoo for the loo! An ode to the commode! Dotty for the potty! It's World Toilet Day!
items.summary: Twenty-five years ago, Jack Sim was flush with excitement. (Please pardon the pun.) The Singapore entrepreneur was looking for a meaningful project and came upon this thought from the prime minister: "He said we should measure our graciousness according to the cleanliness of our public toilets," Sim recalls. Thus was born World Toilet Day. The goal was more than cleanliness. It was access, too — billions of people do not have a safe and sanitary toilet to use. Enshrined as an official U.N. day in 2013, World Toilet Day aims to get people talking and thinking about a topic that maybe is a taboo in polite conversation.

items.title: Big bets against AI debt, from CoreWeave to Oracle and the Mag 7, could soon hit the ETF market
items.summary: Concerns about balance sheets and valuations in the artificial intelligence sector have hit the market hard since October, and investors who have shorted publicly traded tech companies in the AI trade have profited. Most investors don't think as much about "shorting" debt, but there will be a way through exchange-traded funds to profit from widening credit default swap spreads of top AI companies. Both Tuttle Capital and Defiance ETFs have filed for funds that target the credit default swaps of companies closely linked to the AI trade, from CoreWeave and Oracle to the Magnificent Seven: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms, Microsoft Corporation, Nvidia, Tesla, and Apple.

items.title: Bull Shows Intel Xeon Diamond Rapids Package at SC26
items.summary: Intel is doing a mini launch of its next-generation server CPU (or something thereabouts at SC26). There are many systems on the floor, but one, the Bull Sequana XH31600, actually showed Diamond Rapids packages. Starting off, here is the Bull compute blade with blind mate power and liquid at the rear, networking in front, and four Intel Xeon Diamond Rapids packages up front. Just ot be clear about what you are seeing, these are two dual-socket compute nodes with Intel Diamond Rapids, each with 16-channel memory.

items.title: Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices
items.summary: Models are now good enough to work for hours or even days on their own. You don’t have to watch over every thing they do, but you still need to be able to check in, no matter where you are. An agent can’t live only inside one application. The work should continue even If you close a window or switch devices. In GitHub Copilot you can start an agent session in one place and pick it up in another. This session continuity runs on the Agent Host Protocol (AHP), an open standard built first in VS Code and adopted across GitHub.

items.title: Midterms’ ‘blue tsunami’ gives Congress and states an opportunity to take action on climate change – here’s what they could actually do
items.summary: The 2026 U.S. midterm elections are sweeping Democratic majorities into Congress and state legislatures across the country. That’s creating an opportunity to shift the country back to responding to climate change. But faced with a president who staunchly opposes policies that could help slow climate change, what will these leaders with newfound power actually be able to do? Democrats in Congress will have a stronger hand to play in their negotiations with the White House come January, and they may have leverage in pursuing climate policies during negotiations over the federal budget.

items.title: JetBlue Faces $2.5 Million Lawsuit Over Passenger Injury
items.summary: NEW YORK– JetBlue Airways (B6) is facing a $2.5 million lawsuit after a passenger allegedly suffered head and knee injuries when another traveller struck her with a suitcase while rushing to leave an aircraft. The incident occurred aboard JetBlue Flight B6 2126 from Montego Bay, Jamaica (MBJ), to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL). The plaintiff claims the airline failed to remove a disruptive passenger before departure, raising questions about its responsibility under the Montreal Convention.

items.title: The Amazing Inventions of Ancient Greece: From Plato’s Alarm Clock to Ancient Flamethrowers
items.summary: Pla­to’s water alarm clock is just one of the pieces of advanced ancient Greek tech­nol­o­gy explained in the new video above from Lost in Time, a YouTube chan­nel whose look at ancient Roman tech­nol­o­gy we post­ed here on Open Cul­ture last year. Most of the oth­ers were invent­ed for less gen­tle pur­pos­es: we have a nasty-look­ing flamethrow­er on wheels meant to breach stone fortress­es; a “machine gun” able to fire arrows much more rapid­ly than any bow­man; a nine-sto­ry-tall pro­to-tank ful­ly stocked with cat­a­pults and sol­diers ready to swarm a city; and a gigan­tic claw, designed by no less a mind than Archimedes, able to grab and over­turn invad­ing war­ships.

items.title: Fire Retardant Linked to Serious Airtanker Corrosion
items.summary: The National Transportation Safety Board is calling on the U.S. Forest Service to strengthen its corrosion testing requirements for aerial firefighting retardants after an investigation identified extensive damage to two large airtankers. In a report released this month, the NTSB determined that the agency’s existing qualification process failed to adequately evaluate the effects of a magnesium chloride-based retardant on aircraft structures. Corrosion Found on Airtankers The investigation involved a British Aerospace BAe-146 operated by Neptune Aviation Services and an MD-87 operated by Aero Air.

items.title: As overdose deaths fall, White House makes misleading claims about who deserves credit
items.summary: When the White House announced big improvements in the number of people dying from fatal drug overdoses earlier this week, officials pointed to hopeful new data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention showing U.S. drug deaths have plunged to their lowest level in roughly a decade, saving nearly 50,000 lives each year. But leading drug policy researchers say the White House statement also made misleading claims about the timing and cause of the remarkable public health success when it said that gains occurred primarily over the last 18 months due to policies enacted under President Trump's leadership.

items.title: The Psychedelic Animated Video for Kraftwerk’s “Autobahn” (1979)
items.summary: Ah, yes, “Autobahn.” From the moment the door slams and the ignition starts, prog rockers and pre-new wavers know a journey is afoot. Though Kraftwerk had already made three albums, and the band members still looked like well-meaning, bookish hippies, 1974’s “Autobahn” is considered Year Zero for the denizens of the Electric Café, the four German robots who made human music with machines. This cel-drawn animation by Roger Mainwood was made in 1979 to promote “Autobahn,” after most of the culture had caught up with the song, and it’s now bopping around pop culture again.

items.title: Ryanair Passengers Left Unable to Use Toilets During 80 Minutes of Pilot Breaks
items.summary: NEW YORK – A passenger has raised concerns about Ryanair (FR) flight procedures after allegedly being unable to access toilets during extended cockpit absences by pilots on a flight from Paphos (PFO), Cyprus, to London Stansted (STN). Author and meditation teacher Guru Rajesh Ananda said the incident occurred aboard flight FR3132 on October 27, 2026, and questioned the airline’s handling of passenger welfare and flight deck security. Ananda claimed that both pilots left the cockpit separately for approximately 40 minutes each, while passengers remained seated and could not move freely around the cabin.

items.title: Viagogo may have broken law on hidden fees, watchdog provisionally finds
items.summary: Ticket-reselling site Viagogo may have broken the law on hidden fees, the UK's competition body has said in a provisional finding. The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) said it found that Viagogo failed to show consumers the total price upfront when they were buying tickets "and added fees later in the process, a practice known as drip pricing". The CMA added that this was an initial finding, and it should not be assumed that the company had actually broken the law. In a statement, Viagogo said it was co-operating fully with the CMA, adding that the investigation was continuing and "no final findings have been made".

items.title: Nurse spends $50,000 on a new car to drive home after US flights grounded
items.summary: A woman splashed out on a $50,000 car so that she could get home during the nationwide air travel stop in the United States, and ended up driving for 27 hours. Back on November 13, travel plans across the United States were plunged into chaos after a nationwide ground stop was put on planes. The stoppage saw 20,000 flights disrupted, leaving passengers to miss getting home, traveling for work, and delayed for at least a day. In true Planes, Trains, and Automobiles fashion, some travellers set out to find alternative modes of transport as a result of the group stoppage.

items.title: Earth Faces Extinction In Netflix’s ‘3 Body Problem’ Season 2 Teaser
items.summary: They haven’t flown 24 trillion miles to negotiate. The alien invasion gets nearer in season two of Netflix’s blockbuster series 3 Body Problem; the first teaser sees Earth potentially on the cusp of extinction. The Emmy-nominated series returns globally on January 14, 2027, only on Netflix. In season two, “As the alien invasion nears, humanity prepares to meet them — on Earth and beyond. While a space fleet embarks on a mission that spans centuries, a secret locked inside of one man’s mind might be humanity’s only hope for survival.”

items.title: Magic Knight Rayearth Anime Casts Hikaru Midorikawa, Kōji Yusa
items.summary: The staff for the new anime of CLAMP 's Magic Knight Rayearth manga confirmed on Thursday that Hikaru Midorikawa is voicing the Rune God Windom. Additionally, the anime's staff previously confirmed on November 12 that Kōji Yusa is voicing the Rune God Ceres. Yui Miura (episode director for Ninja Kamui, Bullet/Bullet ) is making his series directorial debut with the anime, and E&H production is producing the anime. Shigeru Murakoshi ( Zombie Land Saga, Ninja Kamui, Apocalypse Hotel ) is in charge of the series scripts.

items.title: The Best Places to Go in Central and South America 2027
items.summary: This is my fourth year leading our guide to the Best Places to Go in Central and South America, and each time I’m in awe of the final result—our list for 2027 is no exception. We’re talking about a region where the Pacific, the Atlantic, and the Caribbean converge; where the Andes reach for the Amazon; and where strings of puffy volcanoes and postcard-worthy islands stud the map like jewels. Within it all there are thriving cities where cultures ancient and modern collide head-on, and small towns that are timeless in a way that feels increasingly rare.

items.title: Netflix CEO admits app may bury stuff you want to watch under stuff you don’t
items.summary: The streaming wars, or the battle to be the top streaming company, are ongoing, according to Ted Sarandos, a co-CEO of what many would consider today’s frontrunner. items.summary: There are various things that can happen to an aircraft when it ceases flying for good. While many are simply scrapped straight away, others are kept by airlines as training resources or sources of spare parts. Some, however, go on to be repurposed, with the Jumbo Stay hotel at Stockholm Arlanda Airport (ARN) in Sweden being a notable example. In 2009, the retired 747 was reopened as accommodation.

items.title: Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show
items.summary: After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms. When testing the agent, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages that users did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed. items.title: OMA Rethinks Retail Through Craft and Circular Design at Potato Head Bali
items.summary: What if a store invited visitors to consider not just what they’re buying, but how it’s made? At Desa Potato Head in Bali, the new Good Times General Store explores that question through architecture, craftsmanship, and circular design. Created in collaboration with OMA, Potato Head’s first permanent retail space shifts the focus from consumption to discovery, inviting visitors to engage with the materials and processes behind the products. Photography by Sharon Angelia Building on a partnership spanning more than a decade, OMA and Potato Head envisioned the store as an extension of the hospitality brand’s “Good Times, Do Good” philosophy.

items.title: The Best Tech Gifts for Design Enthusiasts
items.summary: Technology has become so thoroughly integrated into our lives that it’s easy to overlook the design behind it. But look beyond the specifications, and you’ll find plenty of objects worth paying attention to: a clock that uses light and sound to mark the passing hours, a digital frame that resembles a printed photograph, and a cassette-playing boombox that brings back the pleasure of physical controls. For this year’s tech gift guide, we’ve selected 18 products that put as much thought into how they look and feel as what they do.

items.title: Dig Your Way Out Next Year in Psychological Horror Title ‘GRINDWORM’
items.summary: Get ready for more subterranean horror gaming next year, as developer/publisher Snail Bite has announced that its psychological horror game GRINDWORM will arrive on Steam on January 18th. To mark the release date announcement, Snail Bite has released a new trailer showcasing the game’s tense gameplay, oppressive atmosphere, and immersive in-world interface. Taking a cue from Iron Lung, GRINDWORM is built around isolation, dread, and the slow erosion of reality. You were late for your shift. Now the tunnels have collapsed, and your crew is missing.

items.title: 42 Years Later, The Terminator's Most Famous Line Is Still The Greatest Sci-Fi Movie Quote
items.summary: "The Terminator" bowed in 1984 but was so ahead of its time it could easily debut today and be just as, if not more relevant. The film's encapsulation of society's collective fear of a technological future gave what would have otherwise been a sci-fi slasher B-movie real depth. Paired with James Cameron's still-developing yet impressive filmmaking skills, honed over years spent toiling for Roger Corman's New World Pictures and a particularly unfortunate experience on 1982's "Piranha II: The Spawning," that remarkable prescience made the film an instant classic that also happened to give its star, Arnold Schwarzenegger, his most memorable catchphrase.

items.title: Mullin: Wave of Tech Failures May Be Linked to AI
items.summary: Artificial intelligence could be playing a role in the cascade of high-profile technology failures seen over the last week, U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Monday. Mullin told FOX News’ Sean Hannity that he spoke with someone in the tech industry, “one guy who is very smart with tech,” who identified AI as a possible culprit. “He said, ‘I believe that it’s the SI, because the programs aren’t designed to work as fast as SI is,'” he said. The individual suggested that the technology’s ability to move fast and fix itself created “ripple effects” that overwhelmed older conventional systems.

items.title: South Korea's top court overturns jail term for former PM Han
items.summary: The South Korean Supreme Court on Thursday overturned a 15-year prison sentence for the country's former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo for playing a key role in the 2024 imposition of martial law by ex-President Yoon Suk Yeol. The case will now return to a lower court, the Seoul High Court, which had sentenced Han to 15 years in prison in May. Han was convicted for helping plan the insurrection by suggesting that Yoon hold a Cabinet meeting to make martial law seem legitimate. He also allegedly tried to collect Cabinet members' signatures on a related document and reviewed orders to cut off power and water to media outlets critical of Yoon.

items.title: Potatoes grown in moon dirt are as nutritious as Earth potatoes
items.summary: Astronauts living in the first permanent lunar base may see a sizable number of spuds on their dinner plates. In a study published today in the journal npj Microgravity, botanists at Oregon State University (OSU) proved it’s possible to grow healthy, edible potatoes in simulated moon soil with the help of everyday worms. Importantly, the team also identified the proper proportions of lunar regolith and compost needed to produce potato yields similar to those grown on Earth. “We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter,” Aymeric Goyer, an OSU botanist and study co-author, said in a statement.

items.title: Mathematicians make a breakthrough in 174-year-old problem
items.summary: While mathematicians technically solved a nearly 175-year-old theorem known as the Four-Color Problem in 1976, the problem continues to vex researchers. For some in the field, their fascination with the perniciously complex concept runs so deep, that they liken their obsession to a lingering disease. But after a decade of analysis, an international team of mathematicians has made the first major breakthrough in the ongoing Four-Color Problem saga in 30 years. At this year’s Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS) conference, investigators laid out the optimal, most efficient algorithm that solves the Four-Color Problem.

items.title: Russia opens investigation after An-12 military crash kills 19 in Siberia
items.summary: Russian military investigators say they have opened a criminal investigation after an Antonov An-12 transport aircraft crashed near Kemerovo in southwestern Siberia on November 17, 2026, killing all 19 people aboard. Russian media outlets reported that the aircraft had been flying from Novosibirsk to Kansk when one of its engines reportedly caught fire. The crew requested an emergency landing at Kemerovo Airport but crashed several miles short of the runway. Witnesses on the ground said the airplane was on fire before it crashed.

items.title: Will Wright's next simulation will use AI to mine content from your memories

Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players' memories. MyMems, which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright's previous projects by "turn the simulation inward," as Wright's Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning.

items.title: 7 Great Sci-Fi Movies That Come Close to Perfection
items.summary: No science fiction movie is perfect. Even the sci-fi movies we say are truly perfect aren't actually perfect because perfection is an unreachable ideal, and when movies get close enough to it, it's easy enough to anoint them. items.title: Arizona Snowbowl kicks off ski season earlier than expected
items.summary: FLAGSTAFF, AZ (AZFamily) — Get ready to hit the slopes! Arizona Snowbowl in Flagstaff announced that it will open for the ski season at 9 a.m. Thursday — a day earlier than anticipated thanks to the amount of snow it got. “Thanks to the incredible efforts of our mountain operations teams and 17 inches of preseason snowfall, we’re opening 24 hours early for skiing & riding!” the ski resort said. Five inches of fresh powder fell over the past few days, and more snow is forecast for this week, according to the resort.

items.title: Maine Aviation Group Launches Effort to Preserve World’s Only DC-3 on Floats
items.summary: A Maine aviation preservation group is working to secure the future of the world’s only A Maine aviation preservation group is raising money to acquire a stake in the world’s only flying Douglas DC-3 equipped with amphibious floats, with plans to keep the historic aircraft airworthy and bring it to major aviation events. The Maine Center for Classic Aviation (MCCA), a nonprofit based at Thompson Memorial Field in Pittsfield, Maine, has launched a $100,000 fundraising campaign to become a shareholder in DC-3 N130Q.

items.title: Cracks in public health grew in 2026
items.summary: It’s tough to tally the injuries or deaths that don’t happen thanks to seat belts, lead testing, smoking bans and vaccines. “It is the invisibility paradox,” says Georges Benjamin, CEO of the American Public Health Association in Washington, D.C. “We are invisible because when our best work is done, nothing happens.” But when disaster strikes — say, an outbreak or a pandemic — people take notice. This year’s outbreaks of measles, Ebola, hantavirus and cyclosporiasis brought recent federal reductions into focus — and exposed cracks in a system that aims to keep people healthy.

items.title: UK defense plan under fire as BAE Systems looks to cut 1,070 jobs
items.summary: The UK’s defense plan has come under fire after British firm BAE Systems announced plans to cut 1,070 jobs, including 940 roles from within its air division. The development comes as BAE Systems said it is looking to “reduce complexity, improve efficiency and ensure every pound invested delivers maximum value and capability back to defense”. items.title: SITA’s Sumesh Patel on how Asia-Pacific airports can handle more with less space
items.summary: Current predictions suggest that Asia-Pacific will account for almost half of the world’s future passenger growth – but its airports won’t be able to double in size to keep up. For SITA (Société Internationale de Télécommunications Aéronautiques), the solution lies in moving passengers, bags and borders through the same space more quickly, and in moving more of the airport journey away from the airport itself. At Passenger Terminal Expo Asia 2026 in Singapore, AeroTime sat down with Sumesh Patel, President for Asia Pacific at SITA, the air transport IT provider, to discuss biometric borders, baggage tracking and how the region is preparing for a future of up to 10 billion passengers a year.

items.title: American to Renovate, Expand Phoenix Lounges
items.summary: American Airlines plans to refresh and expand its three Admirals Club lounges at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport. The carrier said Tuesday that it will add seating, upgrade amenities, and improve food and beverage service across all three spaces in Terminal 4. In the near term, the Admirals Club lounge in Concourse A between gates A19 and A21 will get a new servery area, infrastructure enhancements to support expanded food and beverage offerings, and facility updates to improve the overall customer experience.

items.title: ‘Ancestral’ Book Review: Ramsey Campbell’s Intimate English Horror Chiller
items.summary: Ramsey Campbell turned 80 earlier this year, placing him firmly in the territory of horror’s elder statesmen. After six decades in the game, he’s as productive as ever, still churning out new novels and stories, and more importantly, he’s still got that spark that made him one of the most important horror writers of the last five decades. Ancestral, his latest novel, reads like vintage Campbell, a chilling journey through the weird that’s steeped in English folklore, Gothic themes of dark legacies, and psychological dread.

items.title: Increase in direct cremations since pandemic
items.summary: Funeral directors say there has been an increase in direct cremations, with no mourners in attendance, since the Covid-19 pandemic. Brian Ugalde, whose firm of funeral directors has worked in Cornwall for 135 years, said non-attendance had become more acceptable since the lockdowns when families were not always allowed to attend. He said: "A funeral is a ceremony...a farewell, a celebration... it is for for those left behind," he said. But, he said, direct cremation came after Covid when "the model became acceptable and practical", as well as being cheaper.

items.title: Germany news: Pistorius to visit Auschwitz memorial in Poland trip
items.summary: An 18-year-old in western Germany has been held in pre-trial detention in Germany since August over the alleged plot to carry out a terrorist attack on a mosque, prosecutors have said. The teen, who is from the town of Eslohe in North Rhine-Westphalia, allegedly held far-right extremist views and was planning the attack for late 2026 or early 2027, senior public prosecutor Alexandra Wiese said. "He also directed his racist ideology against people of the Muslim faith," Wiese told public broadcaster WDR.

items.title: The Directing Genius of Akira Kurosawa Explained
items.summary: Generations of Westerners have come to appreciate Japanese cinema through the films of Akira Kurosawa, but many have been shocked to find out that Kurosawa himself isn’t as beloved in Japan as they’d imagined. It’s less that his homeland rejects him than that his work has been regarded there as a somewhat foreign taste. That judgment must have something to it: despite their thoroughly Japanese settings, Throne of Blood, The Bad Sleep Well, and Ran were, after all, Shakespeare adaptations, and Kurosawa spoke openly of structuring his stories in the manner of not just traditional Japanese theater, but also symphonies.

items.summary: Today we are releasing DaisyRose-27B, RadixArk’s first model, built on Qwen3.8-27B and trained with reinforcement learning using Miles. items.title: Why your fine-tuning job takes longer than the FLOPs say
items.summary: Predicting end-to-end fine-tuning time on shared GPU clusters, from 272 production runs. A preview of our upcoming paper, Predicting End-to-End Fine-Tuning Time for Generative Language Models. The full version will be on arXiv soon. GPUs are among the most expensive and scarcest resources in AI today. Anyone running a shared cluster has to decide, every day, which jobs go on which GPUs and in what order. That plan is only as good as the estimate of how long each job will take. When a job finishes hours early, GPUs sit idle until the next one is dispatched.

items.title: How to Plan a Trip to the World’s Largest Ski Resort, Les Trois Vallées
items.summary: Standing at the top of a steep gully, I looked down at the line ahead. A handful of tracks cut through 10 inches of powder to my left, telling the story of the skiers who arrived before me. But I couldn’t help but notice untouched snow under an overhanging cliff face to my right. Before I dropped in, I looked out at the view ahead. I could make out tiny chairlift towers on the snow-capped peaks and ridgelines on the horizon. It felt as if the entire mountain range belonged to the Les Trois Vallées Ski Resort, one of the best—and the biggest—ski destinations in Europe.

items.title: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone
items.summary: New multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. Deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities.

items.title: 'Defense by ChatGPT'
items.summary: We've written a lot about how AI generated writing has collided with – and created chaos for – the legal system in the last few years, from lawyers using it to do their research and filings for them to judges getting extremely fed up with dealing with these attorneys. In some cases, judges have sanctioned offending attorneys thousands of dollars for using AI to do their jobs, and lawyers give endless excuses when they're busted, with some calling it a “cautionary tale." Today's story is about how the DOJ is getting involved: by trying to catch attorneys doing "defense by ChatGPT."
